charts.question: Need is spatially clustered rather than randomly scattered
charts.supported_finding: The tract map and Moran’s I place candidate hubs inside the observed geography of composite need.
charts.interpretation_boundary: Tract centroids and straight-line distance are planning-screen approximations.

charts.question: Service assumptions can reverse the apparent advantage
charts.supported_finding: Radius, need-weight, and coarse-grid sensitivity reveal dependence on spatial scale and access assumptions.
charts.interpretation_boundary: Travel networks, capacity, ACS margins of error, and local site feasibility remain outside the screen.

charts.question: Composite allocation balances multiple dimensions of need
charts.supported_finding: Every strategy uses the same hub count and radius before population and need coverage are compared.
charts.interpretation_boundary: Weights encode a planning priority and require local stakeholder review.
